summary: A fresh admitted replay first diverges at segment 0 step 148 after #monster dispatch reaches polyself.c:dohide. The viper is hiding under the square's only floor object, an unresisted cockatrice corpse. C prints the fatal-mistake message, builds 'hiding under <corpse name>' and calls trap.c:instapetrify, which prints the stone message and enters the death sequence. JavaScript prints the fatal-mistake message but records note_unported('trap.c instapetrify'), so the next pager and cursor differ while RNG stays aligned. GOALS lists dohide as a historical declaration but the source roadmap has no verified completion evidence for it. Implement the complete polyself.c:dohide function and wire the existing instapetrify implementation at the missing source call.

source.branch: Read the complete polyself.c:dohide definition at 1777-1876. In this case hides_under is true, the floor pile contains only petrifying corpses, Stone_resistance is false, and ct is one. C uses cxname on the top corpse, applies an() only for ct==1, appends plur(ct), prints the fatal-mistake message, builds kbuf as 'hiding under <corpse name><plural suffix>', and calls instapetrify(kbuf). JavaScript preserves the same pile test, name and first message, but records note_unported('trap.c instapetrify') instead of calling the existing implementation. C discards the void result; after return from a lifesaving outcome, both paths clear uundetected and return ECMD_TIME.
callers: cmd.c:domonability (890-914) dispatches the #monster command to dohide for a hider; js/cmd.js:domonability calls js/polyself.js:dohide(state).

evidence: Fresh replay: node scripts/scan-sessions.mjs --json --synthetic v51/v51-viper-hide-clean-cockatrice-corpse-action-attempt3. The first screen and cursor mismatch is segment 0 step 148; RNG is still matched. JS records trap.c instapetrify as unported.

Admitted v51 manifest sourceTrace: step 148 is the fatal-mistake pager and stone/death sequence at steps 149-150. The recipe's leftward movement separates starting equipment from the only floor corpse, so the fatal test is the all-petrifying-corpse pile branch.
C source nethack-c/upstream/src/polyself.c:1777-1876 counts the petrifying corpse pile, constructs the exact killer text and calls instapetrify(kbuf); the call result is discarded.
JS source js/polyself.js:dohide preserves the source pile traversal and fatal-mistake message, then records note_unported('trap.c instapetrify') before clearing uundetected and returning ECMD_TIME.

The source roadmap at the selected base reports polyself.c with 9 verified of 34 declarations and has no verified dohide source evidence. The historical GOALS declaration marked dohide ported is inventory, not completion evidence. js/trap.js already implements trap.c:instapetrify and its call to done(STONING).
